content: Acanthosis nigricans is a dermatological condition characterized by the presence of darkened, thickened, and velvety skin, typically occurring in areas of the body where folds and creases are present. The symptoms of acanthosis nigricans develop gradually and are usually limited to changes in the skin's appearance. Over time, affected areas of the skin become dark, velvety, and exhibit prominent markings and creases. These changes are most commonly observed in the armpits, groin, and neck folds, as well as over the joints of the fingers and toes. In less common cases, other areas such as the lips, palms, soles of the feet, or other regions may also be involved. These symptoms are more frequently seen in individuals with cancer. The condition can be caused by obesity, as well as certain endocrine disorders. It is often associated with individuals who have obesity-related diabetes. Additionally, specific medications, particularly hormones like human growth hormone or oral contraceptives, can trigger the development of acanthosis nigricans. Severe cases may also occur in individuals with lymphoma or cancers of the gastrointestinal or genitourinary tracts. Acanthosis nigricans can affect otherwise healthy individuals or may be linked to underlying medical conditions. In some cases, the condition is inherited genetically. It is most commonly observed in individuals of African descent, partly because the changes are more noticeable on darker skin. Diagnosis is typically made by a healthcare provider through a visual examination of the skin. In unusual cases, a skin biopsy may be required. If no clear cause is identified, further testing may be necessary. This may include blood tests, endoscopy, or imaging studies such as X-rays to rule out diabetes or cancer as potential causes. It is important to seek medical attention if you notice areas of thickened, dark, and velvety skin developing. Treatment is generally not required for acanthosis nigricans itself, as it primarily affects the skin's appearance. However, addressing any underlying medical condition that may be causing the skin changes is crucial. For cases related to obesity, weight loss often leads to an improvement in the condition. Acanthosis nigricans often resolves or fades if the underlying cause is identified and treated effectively.
